clue.text: Bird for dinner? Make haste with pan!

indicators.note: to make something of the letters is to build a new word out of them in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A cook is told to hurry up with the pan because the game bird is wanted for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: This game bird is commonly shot and roasted, so it is a bird served at the dinner table, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Russian emperor lies in great sarcophagus

indicators.note: something that lies in a container is tucked inside it, so the letters sit within the following words

parts.note: the end of great runs into the start of sarcophagus

explanation.surface: A dead Russian ruler rests inside a huge stone coffin.
explanation.definitionFit: The title was used by the monarchs of Russia before the 1917 revolution, the Russian equivalent of an emperor.

clue.text: Write Bergman in diagram

parts.note: taken as written
a grid is a diagram of squares, like a crossword's

explanation.surface: An instruction to write the name Bergman into a diagram.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a crossword instruction; Ingrid Bergman was the Swedish star of Casablanca.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergman stands for the film actress whose first name this is, a definition by famous example.

clue.text: Loyal, being nuts to get up while carrying a child

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading the word from bottom to top, backwards
something carrying another thing holds it inside itself

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
CH is a standard abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: Someone loyal, though crazy, has to stand up while holding a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' reads as crazy in the surface, but it is just the word to be turned; in a down entry 'get up' means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A staunch supporter is firmly faithful and dependable, a direct synonym for loyal.

clue.text: Friendliness shown with right hand down

parts.note: right and good both mean proper or correct
to will property is to hand it down to heirs

explanation.surface: Friendliness is displayed by a right hand lowered, perhaps in a peaceable gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right hand' looks like one phrase; the words split as right and hand down.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is kindly feeling and benevolence towards others, a close synonym for friendliness.

clue.text: Prevailing mood provides master with hope

indicators.note: the clue says the letters provide the answer, that is, are worked up into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster full of hope sets the general tone of the place.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place or gathering is its pervading tone or feeling, the prevailing mood.

clue.text: No. 1 sailor turning up for allowance

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the run of letters is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the abbreviation for number, without its dot
the Roman numeral for one
tar is an old slang word for a sailor

explanation.surface: The top sailor is coming forward to collect his allowance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. 1 sailor' reads as a leading seaman, but it splits into three pieces that are then turned round together.
explanation.definitionFit: A ration is a fixed portion of food or goods that each person is allowed, so it is an allowance.

clue.text: This tree may still make you laugh

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tree bearing glossy brown nuts

definitions.note: the definition is a description of the noun: a joke so old it may still raise a laugh
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a stale, overfamiliar joke

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as if a tree were funny; the second half describes an old joke, which might still get a chuckle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a common tree with edible nuts and a hackneyed story or joke told too often.

clue.text: Bandit not at home on principle

parts.note: someone who is out is not at home
a law is a rule or principle, as in a law of nature

explanation.surface: A robber stays away from home as a matter of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlaw is a fugitive criminal living beyond legal protection, like a highway robber or brigand.

clue.text: Just like a blonde!

definitions.meaning: second meaning: light-coloured, of hair or complexion

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' reads as 'simply' in the surface, but it is the adjective meaning equitable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means impartial and equitable, and also pale or light in colouring, as blonde hair is.

clue.text: Petition for plump bird

parts.note: round and plump both describe a well-filled figure
the robin is a small garden bird

explanation.surface: Someone presents a petition on behalf of a fat bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a letter or petition whose signatures are arranged in a circle so no signer appears to head it.

clue.text: Being heart-broken, died showing enmity

indicators.note: something broken is shattered and reassembled in a different order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
D is the standard abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A heartbroken lover died, full of bitterness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart-broken' looks like one word for sadness; the hyphen hides the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hatred is intense dislike or hostility towards someone, which is what enmity means.

clue.text: Wine and fish make an irrelevant topic

parts.note: red is short for red wine
the herring is a common sea fish

explanation.surface: Talk of wine and fish pairings is beside the point.
explanation.definitionFit: A red herring is a distraction that draws attention away from the real issue, an irrelevant matter.

clue.text: Newspaper extract displaying activity of barber

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a piece cut out of a paper

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a barber in the paper; the two halves are independent meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an article cut from a printed paper and also the action of trimming with scissors or clippers.

clue.text: Undergraduate, half dead, taking part in exploit

indicators.note: something taking part in another is placed within it

parts.note: a stunt is a daring exploit or feat

indicators.note: taking only half of a word means dropping its other half

parts.note: taken as written, then halved

explanation.surface: A university student, half dead from exhaustion, joins in a daring escapade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half dead' sounds like exhaustion; here it means keeping the first two of the word's four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An undergraduate is someone studying for a first university degree, a kind of student.

clue.text: Earth's no different from a lot of water

indicators.note: making the letters different means arranging them in another order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A philosophical claim that the planet is no different from the vast sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This sea between Britain and mainland Europe is a large body of salt water, playfully understated.

clue.text: Railway coach with beds for fairy-tale beauty?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a train carriage fitted with berths
second meaning: Sleeping Beauty, someone who sleeps for a hundred years

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as a description: Sleeping Beauty is the great slumberer of fairy tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names an overnight train carriage with berths and anyone who slumbers, famously the princess in the story.

clue.text: Typical human being must be jolly in call up

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it
in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to call someone something is to name them
in British usage jolly means very, as in jolly good

explanation.surface: An ordinary man has to be cheerful when called up for military service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like conscription; it splits as call plus a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyman is the ordinary person who represents humanity at large, from the medieval morality play.

clue.text: Show anxiety about the type of bed

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: to fear is to show anxiety
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone frets over what kind of bed to buy.
explanation.definitionFit: A feather bed is a mattress stuffed with plumage, so the word names a type of bed.

clue.text: Not worried about heartless referee

indicators.note: without a heart, the word loses its central letter

parts.note: ca is short for circa, Latin for about
taken as written

explanation.surface: A footballer is unconcerned about a ruthless referee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a link word but supplies CA; the middle E of REFEREE goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Carefree means free from anxiety or responsibility, so it describes someone who is not worried.

clue.text: Five cutting up fancy bread economically, for example

indicators.note: a knife cutting into a loaf goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other
fancy suggests something elaborately reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Five people slice up a fancy loaf to make it go further.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Economically' sits in the surface as a description of thrifty slicing; with 'for example' it becomes a sample of the part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Economically is a word modifying a verb, ending in -ly, so it is an instance of this part of speech.

clue.text: Old boy watched closely and complied

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
to eye something is to look at it carefully

explanation.surface: A former pupil was kept under close watch and did as he was told.
explanation.definitionFit: Obeyed means followed orders or instructions, which is to comply with them.

clue.text: Take issue with model after work

indicators.note: after tells us which piece comes later, so the second piece is written following the first

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
to model for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Someone objects to a model turning up after the job is done.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppose something is to disagree with it or resist it, the same as taking issue with it.

clue.text: Into battle in World War I, which is outrageous

definitions.text: Into battle in World War I
definitions.meaning: first meaning: climbing out of the trenches to attack

explanation.walkthrough: Soldiers went over the parapet of their trench to attack; the same phrase now means beyond reasonable limits.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase meant leaving the trench parapet to charge, and figuratively describes anything excessive or far beyond acceptable bounds.

clue.text: Inflamed swelling detected in test yesterday

indicators.note: something detected in a phrase has been found concealed within it

parts.note: the end of test runs into the start of yesterday

explanation.surface: A medical test carried out yesterday found an inflamed lump.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed infected swelling on the edge of the eyelid.

clue.text: See me join Salvation Army to get uniform!

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army
taken as written

explanation.surface: A recruiting appeal: watch me sign up with the Salvation Army and be issued a uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uniform' looks like the noun for army clothing, but it is the adjective meaning unvarying.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means unchanging and alike throughout, which is what identical or the same means.

clue.text: Finger twisted hair on forehead

indicators.note: something twisted is bent out of its shape, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: Someone twists a lock of hair on their forehead round a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is hair cut to hang straight across the brow, called bangs in American English.

clue.text: Say "Eat me" like this and you should trounce him!

definitions.note: a clause describing the noun phrase: someone who is easily beaten

indicators.note: like this asks you to rework the quoted words into another order

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder

explanation.surface: A cocky opponent who taunts you to eat him alive is asking to be beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy meat is an informal idiom for a person or team that is readily defeated or exploited.
